fact.thing: year-to-date gap on $10,000 between VFV and its CAD-hedged twin VSP
fact.box: a TFSA or RRSP holding a TSX-listed S&P 500 ETF
fact.claim: VFV and VSP track the same S&P 500 index from the same company, and Vanguard Canada's own pages list the same 0.08% MER for both, so the fee is not the difference. As of November 4, 2026, Cboe Canada shows VFV up 15.12% year to date and VSP up 11.16%, which puts $10,000 in the hedged version about $396 behind the unhedged one. The gap is the currency hedge: VSP strips the CAD/USD move out of the return, and this year that move worked in the unhedged fund's favour. In a year the loonie moves the other way the hedged twin is the one ahead, so this is one year's result, not a rule.

plain.what: VFV and VSP are two funds that both hold the biggest US companies, bought all at once. They come from the same company and cost the same small fee of 0.08%. The only difference is that VSP takes the Canadian-to-US dollar move out of your return, and VFV leaves it in.
plain.so_what: On $10,000 this year, that one difference was worth $396 — VFV grew to $11,512 while VSP grew to $11,116.
plain.do: Look up which of the two you actually hold and write down whether the name says hedged.
